observation.visible_scene: Overhead close view of a pour-over coffee setup: a mint-green cone dripper lined with a white fluted paper filter holds a bed of blooming, foam-topped coffee grounds, resting on a black digital scale atop a dark wooden surface. A thin stream of water falls from above onto the bed, fed by a metallic gooseneck kettle whose curved spout enters from the right edge and whose body is partly visible at the right. A hand wearing a ring sits at the bottom left, gripping the kettle handle. The scale's LCD shows a timer and a weight reading.
visible_changes: A continuous thin water stream pours onto the coffee bed throughout the excerpt; the landing point drifts across the bed (left-of-center early, then center, then right, then back toward center), carving and deepening a small crater in the foam.
Surface foam bubbles churn and pop, and the water/bed level in the filter rises gradually as liquid is added.
The scale's weight value climbs steadily across the segment (roughly 883 to 976) while the timer advances (about 53 to 55), consistent with ongoing pouring.
The kettle spout and the bottom-left hand shift slightly as the pour is steered; the overall framing and background wood grain remain essentially fixed (no clear camera motion).
outside_clip_unknowns: The onset and completion of the pour (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
The full brewing recipe, total water volume, and what occurs after this segment.
The exact source/identity of the liquid and the kettle's temperature.
uncertain_details: The scale digits appear mirrored/flipped in orientation, so exact numeric values are approximate.
Whether the rising bed level is due mainly to added water or to extraction/bloom expansion is not distinguishable from the frames.
Precise relationship between the bottom-left hand and the kettle (handle vs. resting) is partly out of frame.
